edges.notes: LLVM documents SPIR-V support and workflows (SPIRVUsage.html).
SPIR-V is used as a portable intermediate representation in OpenCL 2.1+ ecosystem (Khronos).
Vulkan consumes SPIR-V for shader modules (Khronos Vulkan specification).
OpenGL 4.6-era SPIR-V extension track (ARB_gl_spirv); GLSL remains the primary shader language surface historically.
Some SYCL / LLVM GPU lowering paths consume SPIR-V for certain device targets (implementation-dependent).
Level Zero specifies SPIR-V module and kernel programming rules (SPIR-V Programming Guide in the Level Zero specification).
WGSL lowering pipelines for WebGPU often target SPIR-V when the native backend is Vulkan (Tint-class toolchains).
